title: Security Assessment Field Guide — Sales & CS (WIP)
summary: Practical cheat-sheet for Sales/CS to respond to customer security questionnaires. Maps common Qs to short answer templates + evidence locations (RBAC v2, audit log schema, SIEM export), plus automation tasks and open questions.
body:
Purpose:
This is a working field guide for Sales and Customer Success when responding to security questionnaires and RFP sections. Focus is on quick, accurate answers + links to concrete evidence. NOT a canonical policy doc (see Confluence link above) — use this to assemble customer deliverables and escalate technical details back to Product/Security when needed.

Audience and how to use:
- Primary: AE/SE/CS for customer questionnaires and pre-sales security reviews.
- Secondary: Solutions Engineers drafting one-pagers and trust-center snippets.
- Use the templates below for first-pass answers. Attach evidence from the evidence repo or provide links to an on-demand bundle.

Quick reference: where evidence lives (internal shorthand)
- RBAC design doc + diagram: confluence/SEC/RBAC-v2 (linked_artifacts)
- Audit log schema spec: repo/platform/docs/audit-log-schema.yaml (attach when requested)
- SIEM export samples: s3://redwood-security-evidence/siem-exports/ (sample files and README)
- Evidence automation status: Jira SEC-412 (see linked_artifacts)

Common questionnaire questions + short-answer templates (copy/adapt):
1) "Do you support role-based access control? Describe."
- Short answer template: "Yes. Redwood implements a principle-of-least-privilege RBAC system (RBAC v2) that separates identity, authentication, and authorization. Roles are configurable at tenant and org levels; built-in roles cover admin, deployer, auditor, and viewer. Policies are declarative and stored in the control plane; enforcement is enforced consistently at API gateway and within the private control plane agent. See evidence: RBAC design doc + sample role CSV and policy dump."
- Evidence to attach: rbac_v2_design.pdf, sample-role-export-2024-10.csv, confluence link to material.

2) "Can you provide logs for administrative actions and user activity? What's retained?"
- Short answer template: "Yes. All control-plane and inference-management events (auth events, role changes, model deploys, rollout decisions) are logged to the audit-log pipeline and retained for 365 days by default for Hosted customers; retention configurable for Dedicated/Private. Logs include timestamp, user id, role, source IP, action, resource path, request id, and outcome. See: audit-log-schema.yaml for exact fields. SIEM exports are available as JSONL bundles on request or via our SIEM integration connectors (Splunk/Elasticsearch/Datadog)."
- Evidence to attach: audit-log-schema.yaml, sample-audit-export-2024-09.jsonl, SIEM-export-readme.md

3) "How do you integrate with customer SIEMs? Provide sample output and mapping."
- Short answer template: "We provide a configurable SIEM export that can push JSONL files to customer S3 buckets or integrate via secure forwarders (TLS) to Splunk/Elasticsearch. Exports map directly to the audit-log-schema fields and include structured fields for easy parsing. Example field mappings and sample JSON export are attached. We also provide a lightweight connector configuration and a normalization mapping for common SIEM parsers."
- Evidence to attach: siem-sample-jsonl.gz, siem-mapping-table.csv

4) "How are logs protected and what access controls exist for evidence?"
- Short answer template: "Audit logs are cryptographically integrity-protected in transit (TLS 1.2+/mTLS where configured) and at rest via cloud provider KMS encryption. Access to log storage is limited to authorized personnel via RBAC and recorded in the same audit logs. For Private deployments, customers control keys and retention. See: encryption-and-key-management one-pager."
- Evidence to attach: kms-integration-notes.pdf, encryption-one-pager-v1.

Mapping matrix (minimal) - fields you can reference quickly:
- RBAC question -> doc to attach -> owner to escalate
  - RBAC architecture -> confluence/SEC/RBAC-v2 -> Aisha Patel
  - Role export sample -> evidence/rbac/sample-role-export.csv -> Marcus Chen
  - Role-change audit events -> evidence/audit/role-change-sample.json -> Lina Alvarez
- SIEM question -> doc to attach -> owner
  - SIEM integration guide -> docs/siem/export-guide.md -> Evan Rios
  - Sample JSONL -> evidence/siem/siem-sample-jsonl.gz -> Security eng oncall

Sales one-pager snippets (copy into customer docs)
- 60-word blurb for trust center: "Redwood Inference provides production-grade controls for secure inference. Our RBAC v2 enforces least-privilege access across control plane and serving runtime; comprehensive audit logs capture administrative and user activity; SIEM-friendly exports and encryption options let you route and retain logs to meet compliance requirements. Contact security@redwood.ai for a tailored evidence bundle."

- 2-paragraph version (for RFPs):
  Redwood’s RBAC v2 separates authentication and authorization and includes tenant-scoped roles, pre-built policy templates and role-export tooling for customer review. Administrative and operational actions are logged to a structured audit pipeline; logs conform to our audit-log-schema and can be exported as JSONL for ingestion into customer SIEMs or shipped to customer-managed storage. For regulated workloads, Private deployments allow customer-managed KMS and on-prem export connectors.

Checklist for assembling an evidence bundle (quick):
- [ ] Confirm customer's delivery method (secure s3, presigned url, or managed portal)
- [ ] Attach rbac_v2_design.pdf or role-export.csv showing role names and counts
- [ ] Attach audit-log-schema.yaml and a 48-hour sample of exported logs (JSONL)
- [ ] Provide SIEM mapping table or Splunk config snippet if requested
- [ ] Add encryption/KMS summary (if Private or Dedicated)
- [ ] Redact internal PII from any attached logs (follow redaction checklist below)

Redaction checklist (minimal):
- Remove full request bodies that contain customer data unless specifically requested and covered by an NDA
- Truncate or hash user tokens and API keys
- Replace customer identifiers with stable pseudonyms (cust-XXXX)
- Confirm no raw model outputs are included in exports without explicit permission

Automation & evidence packaging notes (work-in-progress):
- Goal: one-click evidence bundle from Security Console that zips: rbac CSV, audit schema, 48h JSONL sample, SIEM mapping, and signed README.
- Current state: prototype exporter exists in platform repo (see GH PR in linked_artifacts). Manual run instructions: internal CLI 'sec-evidence export --bundle --days 2 --dest s3://redwood-security-evidence/for-cust-<id>'.
- Open items/risks: need access controls for who can trigger exports; ensure export job logs its own activities to audit logs (SEC-412).

Escalation matrix (who to ping quickly)
- RBAC design / role edge-cases: Aisha Patel (product-security)
- Audit schema questions and samples: Lina Alvarez (security eng)
- SIEM integration/config snippets: Evan Rios (platform eng)
- Evidence automation blockers: Marcus Chen (infra) -> escalate to SEC-412

Open questions (to resolve with product/security team):
- Default retention policy for Hosted customers to be confirmed for enterprise sales decks (is it 365 or 450 days?).
- Do we have an official white-labeled SIEM connector config for Splunk? If not, add to backlog.
- What is the approved phrasing for "encryption at rest" for Private installs (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)?

Notes to self / TODOs for next revision:
- Add a short sample audit-log event with anonymized fields in this doc for quick paste into responses.
- Canonicalize evidence filenames and add pointer that AEs can include the exact S3 path in a bundle.
- Move final templates into the Sales playbook and lock versioning.

Appendix: quick sample (anonymized) audit log event (single line JSON to paste)
{"ts":"2024-10-02T18:22:33Z","request_id":"req-6df8a3","actor":"user:alice@example.com","actor_role":"org-admin","action":"role.assign","resource":"org/123/role/deployer","outcome":"success","ip":"198.51.100.23"}

End of WIP. Add comments inline in Confluence/PR for final language changes.
